clue.text: Tunic a tailor prepared for delivery

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garment made by a tailor is got ready to be sent out to the customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges TUNICATAILOR. 'Delivery' is the clarity of a speaker's words, not a parcel arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker's delivery is the way they pronounce and form their words, which is their enunciation.

clue.text: Judge a royal nipper

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN
something that nips is a biter

explanation.surface: Someone judges a small royal child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nipper' reads as a small child, but here it is something that bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who settles disputes and decides between parties acts as a judge.

clue.text: Every one detailed comes in to eat food

indicators.note: one piece comes in, entering inside another word

parts.note: to take food is to eat it

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, losing its last letter

parts.note: every one of them means each

explanation.surface: Each person arrives in order to have a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts the tail off EACH, leaving EAC, which 'comes in' to TAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a toasted currant bun eaten at teatime is a kind of food.

clue.text: Sailors' register includes Egyptian embroiderer

indicators.note: the outer pair of words includes another piece, which sits between them

parts.note: a ship's sailors form its crew
a register is a list of names
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian, as in E for Egypt

explanation.surface: A ship's roll of crew members has an Egyptian needleworker on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egyptian' gives just its initial, a standard abbreviation; 'register' looks like a verb but is the noun for a roll of names.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel work is embroidery in fine worsted yarn, so one who does it is an embroiderer.

clue.text: Many a crone is on a bender in Sussex

annotationWithheld.why: Many a crone is on a bender in Sussex (5): L (many) + EWES (crones, old sheep) gives LEWES, but no reading found for 'on a bender', which would be left doing no job; no blog parse found
annotationWithheld.clue: Many a crone is on a bender in Sussex

clue.text: A king died carrying basin of pewter

indicators.note: the letters A, R and D carry the basin in front of them, so it comes first

parts.note: a tank is a basin or reservoir for holding water
R is short for rex, Latin for king
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A dying king is carried in a bowl made of pewter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts TANK ahead of A, R and D. 'Pewter' can mean a vessel made of that metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonym: a pewter is a vessel of that alloy, and the classic pewter vessel is a beer mug.

clue.text: Greek character's very short in the leg

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket, the half of the field behind the batter's legs
micro means tiny, very short

explanation.surface: A Greek person is described as having very short legs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so 'the leg' gives ON. 'Greek character' looks like a person, but it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet is a Greek character.

clue.text: The winger is not in the team. OK?

parts.note: someone not in the team is outside it
OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: A wing player asks whether being dropped from the side is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: In football an OUTSIDE RIGHT is the old name for the right winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Football position: an outside right is a forward playing wide on the right wing.

clue.text: Posh doctor's fury gives offence

parts.note: U means upper class, a posh usage
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
fury is rage

explanation.surface: An upper-class doctor's anger makes people take offence.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from the old U and non-U distinction in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to take umbrage is to take offence, a feeling of resentment at a slight.

clue.text: Hope to restrict the downfall of a language

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hold it in, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to hope is to wish
a downfall is an end

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to prevent a language from dying out.
explanation.walkthrough: Wendish, also called Sorbian, is spoken by a Slavic minority in eastern Germany; 'downfall' looks like a fall from power but simply means an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Slavic tongue of the Lusatian region of Germany, also called Sorbian, is a language.

clue.text: The winger evades the usual trouble

parts.note: to hedge is to dodge or evade
par is the usual or normal level
a row is a quarrel, trouble

explanation.surface: A wing player dodges the ordinary difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: After 7-down, 'The winger' reads as a footballer again, but this time it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the dunnock, a small brown songbird, flies on wings, so it is a winger.

clue.text: Composer keeps a ton of jade

indicators.note: one word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer

explanation.surface: A composer holds on to a large amount of jade stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jade' looks like the green stone, but it is the verb meaning to weary by excess.
explanation.definitionFit: To jade is to tire by overindulgence, and to glut someone with too much is to sate them.

clue.text: Namely, sailor's free of rough skin

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for namely
AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
to be rid of something is to be free of it

explanation.surface: A sailor turns out to have no rough skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical adjective: a scabrid surface is rough and scurfy, like rough skin.

clue.text: There's gravity in woeful song of farewell

indicators.note: one piece is put in another

parts.note: woeful means dreadful, dire
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A sad parting song has a serious, solemn air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gravity' looks like solemnity, but it is the physics symbol G.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament sung at a funeral is a song of farewell to the dead.

clue.text: Rudeness becomes folly right away

indicators.note: the word right is sent away, removed from the longer word

parts.note: folly is foolishness, imprudence

explanation.surface: Bad manners become foolish behaviour straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately', but it means take R away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cheeky disrespect or insolence is rudeness.

clue.text: Freeloading act is a rip-off

indicators.note: off means bad or wrong, so these letters go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: Sponging off others is denounced as a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges ACTISARIP; 'rip-off' looks like one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Living off a host like a parasite is freeloading.

clue.text: The scorer fouled up in New York

indicators.note: something fouled up is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A scorekeeper makes a mess of things in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fouled up' rearranges THESCORER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a city on Lake Ontario in upstate New York is a place found in that state.

clue.text: Caught on pliant sort of plant

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
limber means supple, pliant

explanation.surface: A gardener is caught out by a flexible kind of plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ivy and clematis, which grow up walls and supports, are a sort of plant.

clue.text: Old relationship lefty brought to an end

parts.note: ex means former, old
pi is a ratio, the fixed relationship of a circle's circumference to its diameter
a lefty is a left-winger, a red

explanation.surface: A former romance with a socialist has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relationship' looks like a romance, but it is a mathematical ratio.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a licence or agreement that has expired has come to an end.

clue.text: A tug returned fully laden

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tug is a pull

explanation.surface: A tugboat comes back with a full load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PULL into LLUP.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-up weight of an aircraft is its total weight fully loaded.

clue.text: Remains opposed to West African

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
anti means against, opposed to

explanation.surface: The remains are opposed to a man from West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of a people of central Ghana is a West African.

clue.text: Sucker causes strike on training ships

parts.note: to lam is to beat or strike
PE is physical education, training
RN is the Royal Navy, the ships

explanation.surface: A dummy launches an attack on naval training vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe, but it is a fish that sucks on to prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A river lamprey, a jawless fish that clings with its mouth, is a sucker.

clue.text: One forever complaining about priest's clutch

indicators.note: one word goes about, round, the other

parts.note: a griper is one who gripes, a constant complainer

explanation.surface: A habitual moaner grumbles about the priest's handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: GRIPER goes round P.
explanation.definitionFit: A clutch is a device that grips and holds, so it is a gripping mechanism.

clue.text: Roast large mammal

parts.note: to roast someone is to scold them, to rate them

explanation.surface: Cooking a big animal over a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roast' looks culinary, but it means criticise; to rate is an old word for scold.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the honey badger of Africa and India is a mammal.

clue.text: Marchese ignoring a wild fox

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the remaining letters run riot into a new order
ignoring the letter means leaving it out

explanation.surface: An Italian nobleman disregards a wild fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops one A from MARCHESE to leave MRCHESE, which 'wild' rearranges. A marchese is an Italian marquis.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox in the figurative sense is a crafty, cunning person, a plotter.

clue.text: Cheap stuff containing poor material

indicators.note: one word contains the other inside it

parts.note: tat is cheap tasteless goods
bare means meagre, poor

explanation.surface: Cheap goods have poor-quality fabric in them.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT holds BARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a striped satin upholstery fabric is a material.

clue.text: Fruit for the Castilian in the dance

parts.note: the tango is a dance
el is Spanish (Castilian) for the

explanation.surface: A Spaniard dances with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: TANGO holds EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine and pomelo hybrid is a citrus fruit.

clue.text: A liking for the Parisian taken in by fortune-telling

indicators.note: one piece is taken in by, held inside, the other

parts.note: fortune-telling is prediction
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone takes a fancy to a Parisian fooled by a clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: PREDICTION holds LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a preference or partiality is a liking.
